AZ-2026-SB1456.aiSummary: The bill would change the rules for authorized third-party driver license providers in Arizona. It would require these providers to meet set bond, experience, space, and staff rules, and to follow department quality checks. It would also let them do some commercial driver license work if the director allows it and federal law permits.

AZ-2026-SB1428.aiSummary: Arizona law would add new rules for workers' compensation policies with zero estimated exposure, meaning a policy for an employer that reports no payroll exposure. It would require the applicant to sign a statement saying the information is true and that they have no employees, and if they hire someone during the policy period, they must tell the insurer within 60 days. For some construction businesses, it would also require giving contract partners a copy of the policy and notice, and certain insurance certificates would need a web link to check the policy. These rules would apply to policies and related insurance certificates made on or after July 1, 2027.

AZ-2026-HB2995.aiSummary: This law changes how courts handle child custody and parenting time when domestic violence is involved. It says domestic violence must be treated as against the child’s best interests, and it creates a strong presumption against giving legal decision-making or parenting time to a parent who committed it. Courts must look at more kinds of evidence and make detailed findings on the record when they decide these cases.

AZ-2026-HB2960.aiSummary: This law creates a grant program for cities and counties to start or grow veterans' court programs, and it creates a veterans' treatment court fund to pay for them. AZ-2026-SB1624.aiSummary: The bill would change how Arizona handles traffic tickets from photo radar and other photo enforcement systems. It would set a civil penalty of up to $75 for certain civil traffic violations from those systems, and it would say these violations cannot be used to suspend or revoke a driver license or to raise auto insurance rates. It would also keep drivers from having to identify who was in the photo or respond to a notice of violation, and it was later vetoed by the governor.

AZ-2026-SB1246.title: homeowners' associations; foreclosure process

documents.label: SENATE FACT SHEET: 02/20/2026 GOV As Passed Committee

AZ-2026-SB1246.aiSummary: Arizona would raise the bar for a homeowners' association to foreclose on a condo unit for unpaid common charges. It would require the owner to be delinquent for 18 months or owe at least $10,000, and for special charges of $10,000 or more, only the 18-month rule would apply. The bill also says the board should try to contact the owner and offer a payment plan before filing foreclosure. It also changes how some unit owner charges are treated and how payments are applied.

AZ-2026-HB4010.aiSummary: Arizona would create a Board of Genetic Counselors to license and regulate genetic counselors. It requires people to be licensed to work as genetic counselors in the state, with some exceptions for other licensed health workers and federal workers. The board would keep an online list of licensed genetic counselors and set rules for licensing, fees, and discipline.

AZ-2026-HB2379.aiSummary: The bill would require school district governing board members to complete an 8-hour training on school finance and related board duties. County school superintendents or the state education department would provide the training, and school districts could be charged for the cost. It would also add reporting rules and could make some board members in high-risk districts ineligible to run or be appointed again if they do not meet the training rules.
